payload.claim: This is the only test that verifies `attach_run_to_batch` is called with the right arguments, and it runs against a fresh ledger where this is the first batch ever created (batch_id=1) and the first run ever created (run_id=1). Because both ids are 1, swapping the call at saffron/batch.py:134 to `ledger.attach_run_to_batch(batch_id, outcome.run_id)` would still update `runs.batch_id` to 1 where `run_id = 1` — an identical result — so the test would keep passing while the argument order (and thus every real night, where run_id and batch_id differ) would be silently wrong. The test never exercises a case where run_id != batch_id, so it cannot actually confirm which id lands in which column.
